Any field left absent or set to null falls back to the Chinese source text.
source (出处) usually contains a verbatim classical quotation — never translated, no key here.
ingredientsRaw (组成原文) stays Chinese and is shown as-is.

Keep the source's numbered / circled-number structure and blank lines.

1.name: Ephedra Decoction
1.usage: Decoct the four herbs in nine sheng of water, first boiling the ephedra until reduced by two sheng and skimming off the foam, then adding the remaining herbs and boiling down to two and a half sheng. Strain and take eight ge warm. Cover to induce a light sweat; there is no need to take gruel afterward. In other respects, follow the aftercare instructions for Cinnamon Twig Decoction.
1.mainTreatment: Wind-cold exterior-excess pattern from external contraction. Aversion to cold and fever, headache and generalized body aches, absence of sweating with wheezing, a thin white tongue coating, and a floating, tight pulse.
1.function: Induces sweating and releases the exterior, diffuses the Lungs and calms wheezing.
1.appliedTo:
1. This is the representative formula for treating wind-cold exterior-excess patterns from external contraction. Aversion to cold and fever, absence of sweating with wheezing, and a floating, tight pulse are the key diagnostic points. Because it is a vigorous acrid-warm sweat-inducing formula, the Discussion of Cold Damage prohibits it — even when a cold exterior pattern is present — in "sore-afflicted" people, "dribbling-urination" people, "nosebleed" people, and "blood-loss" people, as well as in exterior deficiency with spontaneous sweating, blood deficiency with a "slow pulse at the cubit position," and cases of "generalized heaviness and palpitations" following mistaken purgation.
2. The common cold, influenza, and also acute bronchitis and bronchial asthma that present as a wind-cold exterior-excess pattern may be treated with this formula.
1.notes:
This formula is a vigorous agent for inducing sweating to expel the evil, designed for wind-cold exterior-excess patterns. Physicians through the ages have listed many contraindications for it; broadly summarized, they include:
① Yang deficiency — sweating prohibited
② Constitutional cold with spleen-stomach yang deficiency — sweating prohibited
③ Habitual sweaters — sweating prohibited
④ Sore-afflicted people — sweating prohibited
⑤ Blood-loss people — sweating prohibited
⑥ Nosebleed people — sweating prohibited
⑦ Dribbling-urination people — sweating prohibited
⑧ Yin deficiency — sweating prohibited
⑨ Nutritive-blood deficiency — sweating prohibited

20.name: Mulberry Leaf and Chrysanthemum Beverage

21.name: Ephedra, Apricot Kernel, Licorice, and Gypsum Decoction
21.function: Acrid-cool diffusing of the Lungs; clears heat and calms wheezing.
21.mainTreatment: Exterior evil not yet resolved with Lung-heat cough and wheezing. Persistent fever, cough with rebellious qi and rapid breathing with flaring nostrils, thirst, with or without sweating, a thin white or yellow tongue coating, and a floating, rapid pulse.

22.name: Bupleurum and Kudzu Decoction to Release the Muscle Layer
22.function: Releases the muscle layer and clears heat. This pattern lies in the muscle layer of the exterior, a combined disease of all three yang channels — greater yang, yang brightness, and lesser yang.
22.mainTreatment: Wind-cold common cold that has become constrained and transformed into heat. Aversion to cold gradually easing, mounting fever, absence of sweating and headache, painful eyes and a dry nose, vexation and sleeplessness, a dry throat and deafness, orbital pain, a thin yellow tongue coating, and a floating, slightly surging pulse.

23.name: Bupleurum and Kudzu Decoction to Release the Muscle Layer (Cheng's)
23.function: Releases the muscle layer and clears heat.
23.mainTreatment: Externally contracted wind-heat. No aversion to cold but thirst, a yellow tongue coating, and a floating, rapid pulse.

24.function: Releases the muscle layer and vents rashes. "Measles is a yang toxin," "measles favors coolness," "one never tires of venting rashes." The routine treatment of measles is summarized in three principles: diffusing and venting, clearing and resolving, and nourishing the yin.

25.name: Toxin-Vanquishing Powder

26.name: Schizonepeta and Saposhnikovia Toxin-Vanquishing Powder

26.mainTreatment: Externally contracted wind-cold-damp evils, as well as seasonal epidemic malaria, dysentery, and sores presenting with a wind-cold-damp exterior pattern.

27.name: Granary Powder
27.function: Augments the qi and releases the exterior; vanquishes toxin and stops vomiting.

28.name: Ginseng and Perilla Beverage
28.function: Augments the qi and releases the exterior; regulates the qi and transforms phlegm.
28.mainTreatment: Wind-cold contracted by a deficient person with internal thin mucus. Aversion to cold and fever, absence of sweating, headache, nasal congestion, cough with white phlegm, chest and diaphragm fullness and oppression, fatigue and lack of strength, shortness of breath and disinclination to speak, a white tongue coating, and a weak pulse.

29.name: Renewal Powder
29.function: Assists the yang and augments the qi; releases the exterior and disperses cold.
29.mainTreatment: Yang-qi weakness with externally contracted wind-cold. Aversion to cold and fever with the cold heavy and the heat light, absence of sweating and cold limbs, fatigue and somnolence, a pale complexion, faint low speech, a pale tongue with white coating, and a sunken forceless pulse, or a floating, large, forceless pulse.

30.name: Ephedra, Aconite Accessory Root, and Asarum Decoction
30.function: Assists the yang and releases the exterior.
30.mainTreatment: Lesser yin disease at its onset with, contrary to expectation, fever and a sunken pulse.

31.name: Ephedra, Aconite Accessory Root, and Licorice Decoction
31.mainTreatment: Lesser yin disease. Aversion to cold and body pain, absence of sweating with mild fever, and a sunken faint pulse; or a water disorder with puffy swelling of the face and body, shortness of breath, inhibited urination, and a sunken, small pulse.

34.name: Major Order-the-Qi Decoction
34.function: Urgent purgation to preserve the yin; drastic purgation of heat accumulation.
34.mainTreatment:
1. Yang brightness organ-excess pattern. Constipation with frequent passing of flatus, epigastric and abdominal focal distention and fullness, abdominal pain that refuses pressure and feels hard on palpation, possibly with tidal fever and delirious speech, sweating from the extremities, a dry yellow tongue coating with prickles or a parched black cracked coating, and a sunken, replete pulse.
2. Heat accumulation with watery discharge. Diarrhea of clear water, pure green in color, with a foul odor, periumbilical pain, hard palpable masses on palpation, a dry mouth and tongue, and a slippery, replete pulse.
3. Interior heat-excess patterns such as heat collapse, spasm disorder, or mania.

35.name: Rhubarb and Moutan Decoction
35.function: Drains heat and breaks up stasis; dissipates clumps and reduces swelling.
35.mainTreatment: Onset of intestinal abscess with damp-heat and stasis stagnation. Pain in the right lower abdomen that refuses pressure, pain like strangury on palpation, or local swelling and clumping, or the right leg flexed and unable to straighten (straightening intensifies the pain), normal urination, intermittent fever, spontaneous sweating and aversion to cold, a thin greasy yellow tongue coating, and a slippery, rapid pulse.

36.name: Warm the Spleen Decoction
36.function: Purges cold accumulation; warms and tonifies the Spleen yang.
36.mainTreatment: Yang-deficiency cold-accumulation pattern. Abdominal pain and constipation, gripping bind below the navel with unrelenting periumbilical pain, cold extremities, a white uncoated tongue without thirst, and a sunken, wiry, slow pulse.

37.name: Hemp Seed Pill
37.function: Moistens the intestines and drains heat; moves the qi and unblocks the stool.
37.mainTreatment: Stomach-intestine dryness-heat with spleen-fettered constipation. Dry, bound stool and frequent urination.

38.name: Benefit the River [Flow] Decoction
38.function: Warms the Kidneys and augments the essence; moistens the intestines and unblocks the stool. In this formula bitter orange directs qi downward and relaxes the intestines while cimicifuga raises the clear yang — combined, they join descent with ascent, embodying the idea of first raising in order to descend. Alisma enters the Kidneys to drain turbidity, not to drip out water for strangury.
38.mainTreatment: Kidney-yang weakness with insufficiency of essence and fluids. Constipation, clear profuse urine, sore weak lower back and knees, dizzy head and eyes, a pale tongue with white coating, and a sunken, slow pulse.

39.name: Ten-Jujube Decoction
39.function: Drives out water and thin mucus by drastic purgation.
39.mainTreatment:
1. Suspended thin mucus. Cough and expectoration with pain radiating to the chest and rib-sides, hard distended fullness below the Heart, dry heaves and shortness of breath, headache and dizziness, or pulling pain in the chest and back with inability to catch the breath, a slippery tongue coating, and a sunken, wiry pulse.
2. Edema. Swelling of the whole body, worse below the waist, abdominal distention with wheezing and fullness, and inhibited urination and defecation.

40.name: Yellow Dragon Decoction
40.function: Purges to unblock the stool; tonifies the qi and nourishes the blood.
40.mainTreatment: Yang brightness organ-excess with qi and blood insufficiency. Diarrhea of clear water pure green in color, or constipation, epigastric and abdominal distention and fullness, abdominal pain that refuses pressure, fever and thirst, spiritual fatigue and scant qi, delirious speech, in severe cases picking at bedclothes and grasping at the air, clouded spirit and cold limbs, a parched yellow or parched black tongue coating, and a deficient pulse.

41.name: Minor Bupleurum Decoction
41.function: Harmonizes and resolves the lesser yang.
41.mainTreatment:
1. Cold-damage lesser yang pattern. Alternating chills and fever, fullness and discomfort in the chest and rib-sides, a taciturn disinclination to eat or drink, vexation with a tendency to vomit, a bitter taste, a dry throat, dizzy vision, a thin white tongue coating, and a wiry pulse.
2. Heat entering the blood chamber. In a woman with cold damage whose menses have just stopped, chills and fever occurring at set times.
3. Jaundice, malaria, and miscellaneous internal-damage disorders presenting with a lesser yang pattern.

42.name: Major Bupleurum Decoction
42.function: Harmonizes and resolves the lesser yang; drains interior heat accumulation.
42.mainTreatment: Combined lesser yang and yang brightness disease. Alternating chills and fever, fullness and discomfort in the chest and rib-sides, incessant vomiting, a stifled mild vexation, hard focal distention below the Heart, or fullness and pain below the Heart, constipation or hot diarrhea, a yellow tongue coating, and a wiry, rapid, forceful pulse.

43.name: Sweet Wormwood and Scutellaria Decoction to Clear the Gallbladder
43.function: Clears the Gallbladder and disinhibits dampness; harmonizes the Stomach and transforms phlegm.
43.mainTreatment: Lesser yang damp-heat pattern. Malaria-like chills and fever with the cold light and the heat heavy, a bitter taste and diaphragm oppression, vomiting of sour bitter fluid or of sticky yellow drool, in severe cases dry heaves and hiccup, distending pain of the chest and rib-sides, scant dark urine, a red tongue with a white greasy coating showing patches of other colors, and a rapid pulse slippery on the right and wiry on the left.

44.name: Frigid Extremities Powder
44.function: Vents the evil and resolves constraint; courses the Liver and regulates the Spleen.
44.mainTreatment:
1. Yang-constraint reversal-counterflow pattern. Cool extremities, or abdominal pain, or diarrhea with a heavy sensation, and a wiry pulse.
2. Liver-Spleen qi constraint pattern. Distending oppression of the rib-sides, epigastric and abdominal pain, and a wiry pulse.

45.name: Important Formula for Painful Diarrhea
45.function: Tonifies the Spleen and softens the Liver; dispels dampness and stops diarrhea.
45.mainTreatment: Painful diarrhea from Spleen deficiency with Liver overactivity. Borborygmus and abdominal pain, loose stool, pain that always precedes the diarrhea and eases afterward, a thin white tongue coating, and a pulse discordant at both bar positions — wiry on the left and moderate on the right.

46.name: Modified Polygonatum Odoratum Decoction
46.function: Enriches the yin and clears heat; induces sweating and releases the exterior.
46.mainTreatment: Yin-deficiency wind-heat exterior contraction. Headache and fever, mild aversion to wind-cold, absence of sweating or scant sweating, cough, vexation, thirst, a dry throat, a red tongue, and a rapid pulse.

47.name: Polygonatum Odoratum Decoction
47.function: Courses wind and releases the exterior; clears heat and nourishes the yin.
47.mainTreatment: Wind-warmth disease with a floating pulse at both the yin and yang positions. Sweating and generalized heaviness, labored breathing that must become wheezing, numbness, a taciturn disinclination to sleep; purging causes difficult urination, sweating causes delirious speech, adding fire-needling causes deafness and difficulty speaking, and purging alone causes fecal and urinary incontinence.

48.name: Scallion and Seven-Ingredient Beverage
48.function: Nourishes the blood and releases the exterior. When a blood-deficient person also has an exterior pattern, failing to sweat leaves the evil unresolved, yet sweating risks either no sweat or a sweat that further injures the yin-blood and gives rise to other patterns — so one nourishes the blood to supply the source of sweat, and effuses the exterior to resolve the outside evil.
48.mainTreatment: Yin-blood depletion after illness, or exterior evil contracted after blood loss (hematemesis, blood in the stool, coughing of blood, nosebleed), with poor self-care. Headache and fever, mild chills without sweating, a tender tongue with a thin or absent coating, and a floating, thin pulse or a floating, hollow pulse.

49.name: Minor Order-the-Qi Decoction
49.mainTreatment: Yang brightness organ-excess pattern. Delirious speech, tidal fever, constipation, chest and abdominal focal distention and fullness, an old yellow tongue coating, and a slippery, hurried pulse.

50.name: Regulate the Stomach and Order-the-Qi Decoction
50.mainTreatment: Yang brightness disease with Stomach-intestine dryness-heat. Constipation, thirst and vexation, steaming fever, or abdominal distention and fullness, or delirious speech, a proper yellow tongue coating, and a slippery, rapid pulse.

51.name: Compound Major Order-the-Qi Decoction
51.function: Unblocks the interior by purgation; moves the qi and invigorates the blood.
51.mainTreatment: Simple intestinal obstruction of the yang brightness organ-excess type with pronounced qi distention.

52.name: Major Sinking-into-the-Chest Decoction
52.function: Drains heat, expels water, and breaks up clumping.
52.mainTreatment: Chest-bind pattern. Hard fullness and pain from below the Heart to the lower abdomen so severe it cannot be approached, constipation, mild tidal fever in the late afternoon, or shortness of breath with agitation and vexation, a dry tongue with thirst, and a sunken, tight pulse that is forceful on pressure.

55.name: Appendix Stasis-Transforming Decoction
55.function: Transforms stagnation and unblocks binds; clears heat and resolves toxicity.
55.mainTreatment: Acute appendicitis of the stasis-stagnation type. Low fever, epigastric and abdominal distention and oppression, belching with reduced appetite, nausea and acid regurgitation, abdominal pain — periumbilical or fixed in location — that refuses pressure, possibly with a palpable mass, constipation, dark urine, a white greasy tongue coating, and a wiry-tight, choppy, or thin pulse.

56.name: Appendix Heat-Clearing and Transforming Decoction
56.function: Clears heat and resolves toxicity; moves the qi and invigorates the blood.
56.mainTreatment: Acute appendicitis in the heat-accumulation stage. Fever worse in the afternoon, a dry thirsty mouth, severe abdominal pain, poor appetite, constipation, and dark reddish urine.

57.name: Appendix Heat-Resolving Decoction
57.function: Clears heat and resolves toxicity; reduces swelling and unblocks binds.
57.mainTreatment: Acute appendicitis in the heat-toxin stage. Fever with or without aversion to cold, a dry thirsty mouth, a red face and eyes, dry lips and tongue, nausea and inability to eat, abdominal distention and pain that refuses pressure, constipation, dark astringent urine or painful urination, a crimson tongue with a yellow greasy or yellow rough coating, and a surging, large, slippery, rapid or wiry, rapid pulse.

58.name: Rhubarb and Aconite Accessory Root Decoction
58.function: Warms the yang and disperses cold; drains binds and moves stagnation. Because cold-excess binds internally, the yang qi does not flow through — so warm the yang and disperse cold; because cold accumulation blocks the intestinal tract and conveyance fails — so drain binds and move stagnation.
58.mainTreatment: Cold-accumulation abdominal pain. Constipation and abdominal pain, one-sided pain below the rib-side, fever, cool extremities, a white greasy tongue coating, and a wiry, tight pulse.

59.name: Three-Substance Decoction for Emergencies
59.function: Drives out cold accumulation by purgation.
59.mainTreatment: Cold-excess abdominal pain. Sudden distending pain of the Heart and abdomen, pain like an awl piercing, hurried breathing and a clenched mouth, and constipation.

60.name: Moisten the Intestines Pill
60.function: Moistens the intestines and unblocks the stool; invigorates the blood and dispels wind.
60.mainTreatment: Constipation from improper diet and taxation fatigue, or dry bound stool that will not pass, complete loss of appetite, and wind-bind or blood-bind patterns.

61.name: Five-Seed Pill
61.function: Moistens the intestines and unblocks the stool.
61.mainTreatment: Fluid-desiccation constipation. Dry stool that is difficult and rough to pass, as well as constipation from blood deficiency in the elderly or after childbirth.

62.name: Control Mucus Special Pill
62.function: Dispels phlegm and drives out thin mucus.
62.mainTreatment: Phlegm-drool lodged above and below the Heart and diaphragm; or sudden unbearable hidden pain of the chest, back, limbs, neck, lower back, or hips, with pulling, hooking pain of the sinews and bones that shifts about; or unbearable headache; or clouded lethargy with excessive sleep; or tastelessness of food, thick sticky drool, a sawing sound in the throat at night, and copious drooling.

63.name: Boats and Carts Pill
63.function: Moves the qi and drives out water.
63.mainTreatment: Edema and water distention. Thirst, coarse breathing, a firm abdomen, constipation and inhibited urination, and a sunken, rapid, forceful pulse.

64.name: Yu's Merit Powder
64.function: Drives out water to unblock the stool; moves the qi and reduces swelling.
64.mainTreatment: Yang-type water. Generalized edema, abdominal distention with wheezing and fullness, constipation, inhibited urination, and a sunken, forceful pulse.

65.name: Guide Out Water Pill
65.function: Drains heat and drives out water.
65.mainTreatment: Edema. Generalized puffy swelling, inhibited urination and defecation, thirst, dark urine, a yellow tongue coating, and a rapid pulse; or damp-heat lumbar pain, or phlegm-damp flowing about with body pain.

66.function: Enriches the yin and increases the fluids; drains heat and unblocks the stool.
66.mainTreatment: Heat accumulation with yin depletion. Dry stool that will not pass and does not respond to purgation, epigastric and abdominal distention and fullness, a dry mouth and parched lips, a red tongue with yellow coating, and a thin, rapid pulse.

67.name: Order-the-Qi and Nourish the Nutritive Decoction
67.function: Drains heat and unblocks the stool; enriches the yin and moistens dryness.
67.mainTreatment: Yin collapse from repeated purgation. Parched lips and cracked mouth, a dry throat with thirst and desire to drink, persistent fever, a hard, full, painful abdomen, and constipation.

68.name: Immature Bitter Orange and Peony Powder
68.function: Moves the qi and harmonizes the blood.
68.mainTreatment: Postpartum abdominal pain with vexing fullness and inability to lie down; also governs abscesses and swellings, to be taken with barley gruel.

69.name: Rambling Powder
69.function: Courses the Liver and resolves constraint; nourishes the blood and fortifies the Spleen.
69.mainTreatment: Liver-constraint, blood-deficiency, Spleen-weakness pattern. Pain in both rib-sides, headache and dizzy vision, a dry mouth and throat, spiritual fatigue with reduced appetite, or alternating chills and fever, or irregular menses and distending breast pain, and a wiry, deficient pulse.

70.name: Augmented Rambling Powder
70.function: Nourishes the blood and fortifies the Spleen; courses the Liver and clears heat.
70.mainTreatment: Liver-constraint and blood-deficiency generating heat. Vexation and irritability, spontaneous or night sweats, headache and dry eyes, red cheeks and dry mouth, irregular menses, distending pain of the lower abdomen, or astringent painful urination, a red tongue with a thin yellow coating, and a wiry, deficient, rapid pulse.

71.name: Black Rambling Powder
71.function: Courses the Liver, fortifies the Spleen, nourishes the blood, and regulates menstruation.
71.mainTreatment: Liver-Spleen blood deficiency. Abdominal pain around the menses and a wiry, deficient pulse.

72.name: Pinellia Decoction to Drain the Epigastrium
72.function: Balances cold and heat; dissipates clumping and eliminates focal distention.
72.mainTreatment: Focal distention from cold and heat mutually binding. Focal distention below the Heart that is full but not painful, or vomiting, borborygmus and diarrhea, and a greasy, slightly yellow tongue coating.

73.name: Fresh Ginger Decoction to Drain the Epigastrium
73.function: Harmonizes the Stomach and reduces focal distention; disperses and scatters water-qi.
73.mainTreatment: Focal distention from water and heat mutually binding. Hard focal distention below the Heart, dry belching with a foul food odor, borborygmus and diarrhea.

74.name: Licorice Decoction to Drain the Epigastrium
74.function: Harmonizes the Stomach and supplements the middle; directs rebellious qi downward and reduces focal distention.
74.mainTreatment: Focal distention from Stomach-qi weakness. Diarrhea dozens of times a day with undigested food, borborygmus, hard full focal distention below the Heart, dry heaves, and vexation with inability to rest.

75.name: Coptis Decoction
75.function: Regulates cold and heat together; harmonizes the Stomach and directs rebellious qi downward.
75.mainTreatment: Heat above and cold below. Heat in the chest and evil qi in the Stomach, abdominal pain, and a desire to vomit.

76.name: Compound Major Bupleurum Decoction
76.function: Harmonizes and resolves the lesser yang; regulates the qi and drains heat.
76.mainTreatment: Abdominal-cavity infection following the relief of an acute ulcer perforation. Tenderness in the upper abdomen and right lower abdomen, borborygmus, dry stool, fever, a yellow tongue coating, and a rapid pulse.

77.name: Surging Wind and Vanquish Toxin Powder
77.function: Courses wind and releases the exterior; clears heat and unblocks the stool.

Aversion to cold with high fever and absence of sweating, dizzy head and eyes, red painful eyes, a bitter taste and dry tongue, throat discomfort, thick sticky nasal mucus and drool, constipation, dark astringent urine, a yellow greasy tongue coating, and a forceful, rapid pulse. 78.name: Kudzu, Scutellaria, and Coptis Decoction
78.function: Releases the exterior and clears the interior.
78.mainTreatment: Hot diarrhea. Fever with diarrhea, vexing heat in the chest and epigastrium, a parched mouth with thirst, wheezing with sweating, a red tongue with yellow coating, and a rapid or hurried pulse.

79.name: Dredging and Cutting Beverage
79.function: Drives out water by purgation; courses wind and effuses the exterior.
79.mainTreatment: Yang-type water excess pattern. Generalized edema, wheezing, thirst, and inhibited urination and defecation.

80.name: White Tiger Decoction
80.mainTreatment: Yang brightness qi-level heat exuberance. Vigorous fever with a red face, vexing thirst with a desire to drink, sweating with aversion to heat, and a surging, large, forceful pulse.

81.name: White Tiger plus Ginseng Decoction
81.function: Clears heat, augments the qi, and generates fluids.
81.mainTreatment: After sweating, vomiting, or purging, interior heat blazing with the four great signs; or a White Tiger Decoction pattern with slight aversion to cold on the back, or thirst not relieved by drinking, or a floating, large, hollow pulse; and summerheat disorders with high fever from dual injury of qi and fluids.

82.name: White Tiger plus Cinnamon Twig Decoction
82.function: Clears heat, unblocks the collaterals, and harmonizes the nutritive and protective qi.
82.mainTreatment: Warm-malaria with a pulse that seems normal, no chills but only fever, vexing joint pain, and periodic vomiting; also wind-damp-heat painful obstruction with vigorous fever, coarse breathing and agitation, swollen painful joints, thirst, and a white tongue coating with a wiry, rapid pulse.

83.name: White Tiger plus Atractylodes Decoction
83.mainTreatment: Damp-warmth disease. Fever with chest focal distention, profuse sweating, a red tongue with a white greasy coating; also wind-damp-heat painful obstruction with vigorous fever and swollen painful joints.

84.name: Lophatherum and Gypsum Decoction
84.function: Clears heat and generates fluids; augments the qi and harmonizes the Stomach.
84.mainTreatment: Lingering heat after cold-damage, warm-disease, or summerheat disease, with dual injury of qi and fluids. Fever with profuse sweating, vexation and oppression of the Heart and chest, rebellious qi with a desire to vomit, a dry mouth with a desire to drink, or deficiency-vexation and sleeplessness, a red tongue with scant coating, and a deficient, rapid pulse.

85.name: Clear the Nutritive Level Decoction
85.function: Clears the nutritive level and resolves toxicity; vents heat and nourishes the yin. As the evil heat has just entered the nutritive level while qi-level signs are not fully resolved, the guiding principle is: "once in the nutritive level, one may still vent the heat back out to the qi level."
85.mainTreatment: Heat entering the nutritive and blood levels. Fever worse at night, spiritual vexation and reduced sleep, intermittent delirious speech, eyes that tend to stay open or shut, thirst or no thirst, faint hidden macules, a rapid pulse, and a dry crimson tongue.

86.name: Rhinoceros Horn and Rehmannia Decoction
86.function: Clears heat and resolves toxicity; cools the blood and disperses stasis.
86.mainTreatment:
1. Heat entering the blood level. Fever and delirious speech, purple-black macules, a crimson tongue with prickles, a thin, rapid pulse, or forgetfulness and mania, rinsing the mouth without a desire to swallow, and easily passed black stool.
2. Heat injuring the blood collaterals. Hematemesis, nosebleed, blood in the stool, blood in the urine, a red crimson tongue, and a rapid pulse.

87.name: Clear Epidemics and Vanquish Toxin Beverage
87.function: Clears heat and resolves toxicity; cools the blood and drains fire.
87.mainTreatment: Warm-epidemic heat-toxin with blazing of both the qi and blood levels. High fever with thirst and drinking, splitting headache, dry heaves and mania, delirious speech and clouded spirit, or macular eruptions, or hematemesis and nosebleed, spasms of the limbs, or reversal counterflow, a sunken, thin, rapid or sunken, rapid or floating, large, rapid pulse, a crimson tongue, and parched lips.

88.name: Spirit-Like Rhinoceros Special Pill
88.function: Clears heat and opens the orifices; cools the blood and resolves toxicity.
88.mainTreatment: Warm-heat summerheat-epidemic with the evil entering the nutritive and blood levels. High fever with clouded delirium, purple macular rashes, ulceration of the mouth and throat, red eyes and agitation, and a purple crimson tongue.

89.name: Coptis Decoction to Resolve Toxicity
89.mainTreatment: Fire-toxin heat exuberance in all three burners. Vigorous heat with vexation and agitation, a parched mouth and dry throat, wrong speech and sleeplessness; or heat-disease hematemesis and nosebleed; or severe heat with macular eruptions, fever with diarrhea, damp-heat jaundice; external abscesses and sores, dark reddish urine, a red tongue with yellow coating, and a forceful, rapid pulse.

90.name: Universal Benefit Beverage to Eliminate Toxin
90.function: Clears heat and resolves toxicity; courses wind and disperses the evil.
90.mainTreatment: Big-head epidemic. Aversion to cold and fever, hot scorching pain of the head and face, eyes that cannot open, throat discomfort, a dry tongue and thirst, a red tongue with a white and yellow coating, and a floating, rapid, forceful pulse.

91.name: Cool the Diaphragm Powder
91.function: Drains fire to unblock the stool; clears above and drains below.
91.mainTreatment: Fire-heat pattern of the upper and middle burners. Vexation, agitation, and thirst, a red face and parched lips, vexing heat of the chest and diaphragm, mouth and tongue sores, or sore throat with hematemesis and nosebleed, constipation and dark urine, or difficult defecation, a red tongue with yellow coating, and a slippery, rapid pulse.

92.name: Sublime Formula for Sustaining Life
92.function: Clears heat and resolves toxicity; reduces swelling and dissipates hardness; invigorates the blood and relieves pain.
92.mainTreatment: Onset of a toxic abscess or sore. Red swelling with hot scorching pain, or fever and shivering chills, a thin white or yellow tongue coating, and a forceful, rapid pulse.

93.name: Five-Ingredient Beverage to Eliminate Toxin
93.function: Clears heat and resolves toxicity; disperses and scatters deep-rooted toxin sores.
93.mainTreatment: Onset of a deep-rooted toxin sore. Fever and aversion to cold, a sore shaped like a grain, hard with a deep root like an iron nail; also abscesses, sores, and boils with red swelling and hot pain, a red tongue with yellow coating, and a rapid pulse.

94.name: Four-Wonders Decoction for Well-Being
94.function: Clears heat and resolves toxicity; invigorates the blood and relieves pain.
94.mainTreatment: Sloughing flesh disorder with blazing heat-toxin. The affected limb dark red and slightly swollen, hot to the touch, ulcerating and rotting with a foul odor, severe pain, possibly with fever and thirst, a red tongue, and a rapid pulse.

95.name: Guide Out the Red Powder
95.function: Clears the Heart, promotes urination, and nourishes the yin.
95.mainTreatment: Heart-channel fire-heat pattern. Vexing heat of the Heart and chest, thirst with a red face and a wish for cold drinks, mouth and tongue sores; or Heart-heat shifting to the Small Intestine with dark, astringent, painful urination, a red tongue, and a rapid pulse.

96.name: Clear the Heart Beverage with Lotus Seed
96.function: Clears Heart fire; augments the qi and yin; stops strangury and turbidity.
96.mainTreatment: Heart fire overactive with dual deficiency of qi and yin and damp-heat pouring downward. Seminal emission and turbid strangury, flooding and vaginal discharge, brought on by exertion; or Kidney-yin insufficiency with a dry mouth and tongue, vexation and fever.

97.name: Gentian Decoction to Drain the Liver
97.function: Clears Liver-Gallbladder excess fire; drains lower-burner damp-heat.
97.mainTreatment:
1. Liver-Gallbladder excess fire flaring upward. Headache and red eyes, rib-side pain, a bitter taste, deafness, ear swelling, a red tongue with yellow coating, and a wiry, rapid, forceful pulse.
2. Liver-Gallbladder damp-heat pouring downward. Genital swelling and itching, sweating of the genitals, turbid strangury, or foul yellow vaginal discharge, a red tongue with a yellow greasy coating, and a wiry, rapid, forceful pulse.

98.name: Drain the Green Pill
98.function: Clears the Liver and drains fire.
98.mainTreatment: Constrained fire of the Liver channel. Red swollen painful eyes, vexation and irritability, inability to lie quietly, dark urine and constipation, a surging, replete pulse; also childhood acute fright wind with heat exuberance and convulsions.

99.name: Tangkuei, Gentian, and Aloe Pill
99.function: Clears and drains Liver-Gallbladder excess fire.
99.mainTreatment: Liver-Gallbladder excess fire. Dizzy head and vision, a restless spirit, delirious speech and mania, or constipation and dark astringent urine.

100.name: Left Metal Pill
100.function: Clears and drains Liver fire; directs rebellious qi downward and stops vomiting.
100.mainTreatment: Liver fire invading the Stomach. Rib-side pain, gnawing hunger with acid swallowing, vomiting with a bitter taste, a red tongue with yellow coating, and a wiry, rapid pulse.

101.name: Fifth and Sixth Heavenly Stem Pill
101.function: Courses the Liver and regulates the Spleen; clears heat and harmonizes the Stomach.
101.mainTreatment: Stomach pain with acid swallowing, and abdominal pain with diarrhea, due to Liver-Spleen disharmony.

102.name: Drain the White Powder
102.function: Clears and drains Lung heat; calms wheezing and stops cough.
102.mainTreatment: Lung-heat wheezing and cough. Wheezing and cough, skin that feels steaming hot especially in the late afternoon, a red tongue with yellow coating, and a thin, rapid pulse.

103.name: Descurainia and Jujube Decoction to Drain the Lungs
103.function: Drains the Lungs and moves water; directs qi downward and calms wheezing.
103.mainTreatment: Congestion and exuberance of phlegm-drool with cough, wheezing, and chest fullness.

104.name: Reed Decoction
104.function: Clears the Lungs and transforms phlegm; drives out stasis and expels pus.
104.mainTreatment: Lung abscess. Mild fever, cough with copious phlegm, in severe cases coughing up fishy-smelling pus and blood, hidden pain in the chest, a red tongue with a yellow greasy coating, and a slippery, rapid pulse.

105.name: Clear the Stomach Powder
105.function: Clears the Stomach and cools the blood.
105.mainTreatment: Stomach-fire toothache. Toothache radiating to the head, hot cheeks, teeth that prefer cold and are averse to heat; or spontaneous gum bleeding; or red swollen ulcerated gums; or swollen painful lips, tongue, cheeks, and jaw; hot foul breath, a dry mouth and tongue, a red tongue with yellow coating, and a slippery, rapid pulse.

106.name: Drain the Yellow Powder
106.function: Drains latent fire from the Spleen and Stomach.
106.mainTreatment: Latent fire in the Spleen and Stomach. Mouth sores and foul breath, vexing thirst with easy hunger, a parched mouth and dry lips, a red tongue and a rapid pulse, and childhood tongue-thrusting from Spleen heat.

107.name: Jade Woman Decoction
107.function: Clears Stomach heat; enriches the Kidney yin.
107.mainTreatment: Stomach-heat with yin-deficiency pattern. Headache, toothache, loose teeth and gum bleeding, vexing heat and dry thirst, a red tongue with a dry yellow coating. Also treats wasting-thirst and rapid digestion with easy hunger.

108.name: Peony Decoction
108.function: Clears heat and dries dampness; regulates the qi and harmonizes the blood.
108.mainTreatment: Damp-heat dysentery. Abdominal pain, stool with pus and blood mixed red and white, tenesmus, hot scorching of the anus, scant dark urine, a yellow greasy tongue coating, and a wiry, rapid pulse.

109.name: Scutellaria Decoction
109.function: Clears heat and stops diarrhea; harmonizes the middle and relieves pain.
109.mainTreatment: Heat diarrhea and heat dysentery. Fever with a bitter taste, abdominal pain and diarrhea, a red tongue with yellow coating, and a rapid pulse.

110.name: Costus and Coptis Pill
110.function: Clears heat and dries dampness; moves the qi and transforms stagnation.
110.mainTreatment: Damp-heat dysentery with pus and blood mixed, abdominal pain, and tenesmus.

111.name: Pulsatilla Decoction
111.function: Clears heat and resolves toxicity; cools the blood and stops dysentery.
111.mainTreatment: Heat-toxin dysentery. Abdominal pain, tenesmus, hot scorching of the anus, dysenteric stool with pus and blood — more red than white, thirst with a desire to drink, a red tongue with yellow coating, and a wiry, rapid pulse.

112.name: Pulsatilla plus Licorice and Ass-Hide Gelatin Decoction
112.function: Clears heat and resolves toxicity; dries dampness, cools the blood, and stops dysentery; nourishes the blood and enriches the yin.

113.name: Six-to-One Powder
113.mainTreatment: Summerheat-damp pattern. Fever with vexing thirst, inhibited urination, or diarrhea.

114.name: Boost the Primal Powder
114.function: Clears the Heart and dispels summerheat; also calms the spirit.
114.mainTreatment: Summerheat-damp pattern with palpitations and fearful throbbing, insomnia, and profuse dreaming.

115.name: Jasper Powder
115.mainTreatment: Summerheat-damp pattern with concurrent Liver-Gallbladder constrained heat.

116.name: Chicken Perilla Powder
116.mainTreatment: Summerheat-damp pattern with mild aversion to wind-cold, headache and head distention, and an unproductive cough.

117.name: Cinnamon Twig, Poria, and Sweet Dew Beverage
117.function: Clears summerheat and heat; transforms qi and disinhibits dampness.
117.mainTreatment: Summerheat-damp pattern. Fever and headache, vexing thirst with drinking, inhibited urination, and sudden turmoil with vomiting and diarrhea.

118.name: Clear Summerheat and Augment the Qi Decoction
118.function: Clears summerheat and augments the qi; nourishes the yin and generates fluids.
118.mainTreatment: Summerheat-heat with dual injury of qi and fluids. Fever with profuse sweating, thirst and vexation, scant dark urine, bodily fatigue and scant qi, listlessness, and a deficient, rapid pulse.

119.name: Clear Summerheat and Augment the Qi Decoction (Li Dongyuan's)
119.function: Clears summerheat and augments the qi; eliminates dampness and fortifies the Spleen.
119.mainTreatment: Constitutional qi deficiency further affected by summerheat-damp. Fever and headache, thirst and spontaneous sweating, fatigue of the four limbs, no thought of food, chest fullness and generalized heaviness, loose stool, scant dark urine, a greasy tongue coating, and a deficient pulse.

120.name: Sweet Wormwood and Turtle Shell Decoction
120.function: Nourishes the yin and vents heat.
120.mainTreatment: Late stage of a warm disease with the evil hidden in the yin aspect. Fever at night that cools by morning, heat receding without sweating, a red tongue with scant coating, and a thin, rapid pulse.

121.name: Clear the Bones Powder
121.function: Clears deficiency heat; abates steaming-bone fever.
121.mainTreatment: Taxation-deficiency fever. Steaming-bone tidal fever, or persistent low-grade fever, emaciation, red lips and cheeks, drowsiness and night sweats, or thirst and vexation, a red tongue with scant coating, and a thin, rapid pulse.

122.name: Notopterygium and Turtle Shell Powder
122.function: Enriches the yin and nourishes the blood; clears heat and abates steaming fever.
122.mainTreatment: Wind-taxation disorder. Steaming-bone night sweats, emaciation of the flesh, red lips and cheeks, afternoon tidal fever, cough and fatigue, and a faint, rapid pulse.

123.name: Tangkuei and Six-Yellow Decoction
123.function: Enriches the yin and drains fire; stabilizes the exterior and stops sweating.
123.mainTreatment: Night sweats from yin deficiency with fire effulgence. Fever and night sweats, a red face and Heart vexation, a dry mouth and parched lips, dry bound stool, dark reddish urine, a red tongue with yellow coating, and a rapid pulse.

124.name: Regulate the Middle Pill
124.function: Warms the middle and disperses cold; supplements the qi and fortifies the Spleen.
124.mainTreatment: Spleen-Stomach deficiency-cold pattern. Cold epigastric and abdominal pain that likes warmth and pressure, spontaneous diarrhea without thirst, aversion to cold and cold limbs, vomiting, no thought of food, a pale tongue with white coating, and a sunken, thin pulse; or yang-deficiency bleeding; or childhood chronic fright wind; or drooling of saliva after illness, or sudden turmoil with vomiting and diarrhea, and chest painful obstruction, all arising from middle-burner deficiency-cold.

125.name: Aconite Accessory Root and Regulate the Middle Pill
125.function: Warms the yang and dispels cold; augments the qi and fortifies the Spleen.
125.mainTreatment: Spleen-Stomach deficiency-cold overwhelmed by wind and cold, with epigastric and abdominal pain, and sudden turmoil with vomiting, diarrhea, and cramping.

126.name: Cinnamon Twig and Ginseng Decoction
126.function: Warms the interior and releases the exterior; augments the qi and fortifies the Spleen.
126.mainTreatment: Greater yang disease repeatedly purged while the exterior signs remained, leading to unremitting hot diarrhea, hard focal distention below the Heart, and both exterior and interior unresolved.

127.name: Regulate the Middle and Transform Phlegm Pill
127.function: Augments the qi and fortifies the Spleen; warms and transforms phlegm-drool.
127.mainTreatment: Spleen-Stomach deficiency-cold with internal phlegm-drool retention. Vomiting with reduced appetite, or loose stool, difficult digestion, and cough with phlegm-drool.

128.name: Minor Construct the Middle Decoction
128.function: Warms the middle and supplements deficiency; harmonizes the interior and moderates urgency.
128.mainTreatment: Taxation-deficiency with interior urgency. Intermittent abdominal pain that likes warmth and pressure, a pale tongue with white coating, and a thin, wiry pulse; or taxation-deficiency with Heart palpitations, deficiency-vexation and unrest, a lusterless complexion, or vexing heat of the palms and soles, and a dry throat and mouth.

129.name: Astragalus Construct the Middle Decoction
129.function: Warms the middle and supplements the qi; harmonizes the interior and moderates urgency.
129.mainTreatment: Taxation-deficiency with interior urgency and multiple insufficiencies.

130.name: Tangkuei Construct the Middle Decoction
130.function: Warmly tonifies the qi and blood; moderates urgency and relieves pain.
130.mainTreatment: Postpartum abdominal pain. Postpartum weakness and emaciation, unremitting abdominal pain, faint shortness of breath, or lower abdominal cramping with pain radiating to the abdomen, and inability to eat.

131.name: Major Construct the Middle Decoction
131.function: Warms the middle and supplements deficiency; directs rebellious qi downward and relieves pain.
131.mainTreatment: Deficiency-cold abdominal pain. Severe cold pain of the Heart and chest, vomiting with inability to eat, cold in the abdomen surging up so the skin rises with visible head-and-foot shapes, pain above and below that will not tolerate touch, a white slippery tongue coating, and a thin, tight pulse; in severe cases cold limbs and a hidden pulse, or gurgling sounds in the abdomen.

132.name: Evodia Decoction
132.function: Warms the middle and supplements deficiency; directs rebellious qi downward and stops vomiting.
132.mainTreatment: Deficiency-cold vomiting. A desire to vomit after eating grain, aversion to cold and a preference for heat; or epigastric pain with acid swallowing and gnawing discomfort; or reverting yin headache with dry heaves and spitting of drool; or lesser yin vomiting and diarrhea with cold extremities and vexing agitation to the point of feeling near death.

133.name: Minor Pinellia Decoction
133.function: Harmonizes the Stomach and stops vomiting; disperses thin mucus and directs rebellious qi downward.
133.mainTreatment: Vomiting without thirst in a person with propping thin mucus below the Heart, and all cases of vomiting where grain will not go down.

134.name: Frigid Extremities Decoction
134.function: Rescues devastated yang and stems counterflow.
134.mainTreatment: Lesser yin disease. Reversal counterflow of the four limbs, aversion to cold with curled-up lying, vomiting without thirst, abdominal pain and diarrhea, spiritual debility with a desire only to sleep, a white slippery tongue coating, and a faint pulse; or yang collapse from mistaken sweating in a greater yang disease.

135.name: Unblock the Pulse Decoction for Frigid Extremities
135.function: Rescues devastated yang and unblocks the pulse.
135.mainTreatment: Lesser yin disease with diarrhea of undigested food, cold within and heat without, reversal counterflow of the extremities, a faint pulse verging on expiry, no aversion to cold contrary to expectation, and a red face; or the diarrhea stops but the pulse does not return.

136.name: Frigid Extremities plus Ginseng Decoction
136.function: Rescues devastated yang and augments the qi; stems counterflow and secures against collapse.
136.mainTreatment: Internal exuberance of yin-cold with reversal counterflow of the four limbs, aversion to cold with curled-up lying, a faint pulse, and recurrent spontaneous diarrhea that has stopped while the remaining signs persist.

137.name: White Unblock Decoction
137.function: Unblocks the yang and breaks up the yin.
137.mainTreatment: Lesser yin disease with diarrhea and a faint pulse.

138.name: Ginseng and Aconite Accessory Root Decoction
138.function: Augments the qi and rescues devastated yang.
138.mainTreatment: Sudden collapse of the yang qi. Cold extremities, dizziness and shortness of breath, sweating, and a faint pulse.

139.name: Restore and Revive the Yang Decoction for Emergencies
139.function: Rescues and revives the yang for emergencies; augments the qi and restores the pulse.
139.mainTreatment: Cold evil striking directly into the three yin channels with severe decline of the true yang. Aversion to cold with curled-up lying, reversal cold of the four limbs, vomiting and diarrhea with abdominal pain, absence of thirst, spiritual debility with a desire only to sleep, or shivering chills, or blue-purple nails and lips, or spitting of drool, a pale tongue with white coating, and a sunken, faint pulse, or even no pulse at all.

141.name: Tangkuei Decoction for Frigid Extremities
141.function: Warms the channels and disperses cold; nourishes the blood and unblocks the vessels.
141.mainTreatment: Blood-deficiency cold reversal pattern. Reversal cold of the hands and feet, absence of thirst, or pain of the lower back, thighs, legs, and feet, a pale tongue with white coating, and a sunken, thin pulse or a thin pulse verging on expiry.

142.name: Astragalus and Cinnamon Twig Five-Substance Decoction
142.function: Augments the qi and warms the channels; harmonizes the blood and unblocks painful obstruction.
142.mainTreatment: Blood painful obstruction. Numbness and lack of sensation of the skin and flesh, and a faint, choppy, tight pulse.

143.name: Harmonize the Yang Decoction
143.function: Warms the yang and supplements the blood; disperses cold and unblocks stagnation.
143.mainTreatment: Yin-type flat-abscess. Diffuse swelling without a head, unchanged skin color, aching pain without heat, no thirst, a pale tongue with white coating, and a sunken, thin or slow, thin pulse; also bone abscess, sloughing flesh, streaming sores, phlegm nodules, and crane's-knee wind that belong to yin-cold patterns.

144.name: Minor Golden Special Pill
144.function: Transforms phlegm and eliminates dampness; dispels stasis and unblocks the collaterals.
144.mainTreatment: Streaming sores, phlegm nodules, scrofula, breast rock, groin lumps, bone abscess, and rat-fistula from cold-damp phlegm-stasis. At onset, unchanged skin color with hard swelling and pain.

145.name: Cattle Bezoar Pill for the Downcast
145.function: Resolves toxicity and disperses abscesses; transforms phlegm and dissipates clumps; invigorates the blood and dispels stasis.
145.mainTreatment: Breast rock, groin lumps, scrofula, phlegm nodules, streaming sores, Lung abscess, Small Intestine abscess, and the like.

146.name: Four-Gentlemen Decoction
146.function: Augments the qi and fortifies the Spleen.
146.mainTreatment: Spleen-Stomach qi deficiency. A pale white complexion, faint low speech, shortness of breath and lack of strength, reduced appetite with loose stool, a pale tongue with white coating, and a deficient, weak pulse.

147.name: Special Achievement Powder
147.function: Augments the qi and fortifies the Spleen; moves the qi and transforms stagnation.
147.mainTreatment: Spleen-Stomach qi deficiency with qi stagnation. Reduced appetite, loose stool, chest and epigastric focal distention and discomfort, or vomiting and diarrhea. Now used for childhood indigestion with Spleen deficiency and qi stagnation.

148.name: Six-Gentlemen Decoction
148.function: Augments the qi and fortifies the Spleen; dries dampness and transforms phlegm.
148.mainTreatment: Spleen-Stomach qi deficiency with phlegm-damp. Reduced appetite and loose stool, chest and epigastric focal distention and oppression, and rebellious retching.

149.name: Saussurea and Amomum Six-Gentlemen Decoction
149.function: Augments the qi and transforms phlegm; moves the qi and warms the middle.
149.mainTreatment: Spleen-Stomach qi deficiency with phlegm obstruction and qi stagnation. Vomiting and focal oppression, no thought of food, epigastric and abdominal distending pain, emaciation and fatigue, or qi-deficiency swelling and fullness.

150.name: Preserve the Origin Decoction
150.function: Augments the qi and warms the yang.
150.mainTreatment: Taxation-deficiency and timidity with insufficient primal qi. Fatigue and lack of strength, scant qi and aversion to cold; also childhood pox with yang deficiency and sunken tops that fail to fill and suppurate.

151.name: Ginseng, Poria, and Atractylodes Powder
151.function: Augments the qi and fortifies the Spleen; percolates dampness and stops diarrhea.
151.mainTreatment: Spleen deficiency with dampness. Failure to digest food, chest and epigastric focal distention and oppression, borborygmus and diarrhea, fatigue of the four limbs, emaciation, a sallow yellow complexion, a pale tongue with a white greasy coating, and a deficient, moderate pulse.

152.name: Aid the Living Pill
152.function: Augments the qi and fortifies the Spleen; harmonizes the Stomach and percolates dampness; disperses food and regulates the qi.
152.mainTreatment: In the third month of pregnancy, when the yang brightness pulse is weak, to secure the fetus. Also treats Spleen-Stomach weakness with reduced appetite and loose stool, epigastric and abdominal distention, nausea and vomiting, emaciation, and lack of strength.

153.name: Tonify the Middle and Augment the Qi Decoction
153.function: Tonifies the middle and augments the qi; raises the yang and lifts the sunken. As the Treatise on the Spleen and Stomach says: internal damage to the Spleen and Stomach injures the qi; external contraction of wind-cold injures the form. What injures the outside is surplus, and surplus is drained; what injures the inside is insufficiency, and insufficiency is tonified. If an internal-damage disorder of insufficiency is mistaken for an external-contraction disorder of surplus and drained, one deepens the deficiency of a deficient patient. Only a sweet, warm formula tonifies the middle and raises its yang.
153.mainTreatment:
1. Spleen-Stomach qi deficiency. Reduced appetite, bodily fatigue and weak limbs, scant qi and disinclination to speak, a pale white complexion, loose stool, and a large but deficient and soft pulse.
2. Qi deficiency with sinking. Rectal prolapse, uterine prolapse, chronic diarrhea, chronic dysentery, flooding and spotting, shortness of breath and lack of strength, a pale tongue, and a deficient pulse.
3. Qi-deficiency fever. Fever with spontaneous sweating, thirst with a preference for hot drinks, shortness of breath and lack of strength, a pale tongue, and a deficient, large, forceless pulse.

154.name: Raise the Sunken Decoction
154.function: Augments the qi and raises the sunken.
154.mainTreatment: Sinking of the gathering qi. Shortness of breath insufficient for respiration, or forced labored breathing resembling wheezing, or breathing seeming about to stop with imminent danger, and a sunken, slow, faint, weak or irregular pulse.

155.name: Raise the Yang and Boost the Stomach Decoction
155.function: Augments the qi and raises the yang; clears heat and eliminates dampness.
155.mainTreatment: Spleen-Stomach weakness with damp-heat lingering in the middle burner. Sluggishness and somnolence, slack limbs, generalized heaviness with joint swelling, a bitter taste and dry tongue, tasteless eating with poor digestion, and irregular stools.

156.name: Jade Windscreen Powder
156.function: Augments the qi, stabilizes the exterior, and stops sweating.
156.mainTreatment: Exterior-deficiency spontaneous sweating. Sweating with aversion to wind, a pale white complexion, a pale tongue with a thin white coating, and a floating, deficient pulse; also for deficient people with an unsecured interstice-and-pore who catch cold easily.

157.name: Ginseng and Gecko Powder
157.function: Tonifies the Lungs and augments the Kidneys; stops cough and settles wheezing.
